content.thinking: Actually the error rate during the incident was below baseline, so the real user-visible impact was latency, not errors—I should be careful not to overstate that. I also want to flag that the cache port assumption comes from prior config rather than verified evidence, and the ClientDisconnected errors seem unrelated to the core issue.

assumptions: The cache was assumed to still be healthy and listening on the original port 6379 - this was inferred from the prior working configuration rather than checked directly against the cache.

The user-visible harm is characterised as latency, not failures: the error rate during the window was at or slightly below the pre-incident baseline, so no requests are attributed to the fault. The short error peak seen mid-window is within the range the service already showed before the deploy.
The scattered 'ClientDisconnected' errors appear both before and during the window and are assumed to be normal shopper behaviour, unrelated to the cache misconfiguration.
Recovery is attributed to the rollback because the service returned to baseline immediately after it; no separate confirmation was made that nothing else changed at the same time.
The alternative reading - that the cache dependency itself failed - was considered and left untested, on the strength of the deploy diff showing io-shop changed its own port value.
The feature-flag provider reported no recent flag changes, so flags were ruled out as a contributing factor.
input.executive_summary: For about six minutes on 27 September 2026, from 16:00 to 16:06 UTC, the account pages in the shop service were noticeably slow. A configuration change released a minute earlier pointed the service at the wrong address for the cache that holds customers' account summaries, so every page had to be rebuilt from scratch instead of being served from the cache. Shoppers loading account pages in that window would have seen pages take several times longer than usual to appear. Pages did continue to load: the share of failing requests during the window was not higher than the normal background rate, so this was a slowness problem rather than an outage. Automated monitoring raised an alert, the change was identified as the cause, and the release was rolled back; the service returned to its normal behaviour at 16:06 and has stayed there. A draft code fix has since been opened for the team to review.
input.root_cause: The 15:59 production deploy of io-shop changed deploy/values-production.yaml so that the summary-cache client pointed at port 6380 instead of 6379. From 16:00 every cache lookup got "connection refused" to cache.io-shop.svc.cluster.local:6380, the cache hit ratio fell to zero, and p50 latency rose from roughly 26ms to roughly 190ms as every account-page render fell through to the slow path. The cache itself was healthy; only io-shop's own config was wrong. Rolling the deploy back restored the correct port and the service returned to baseline.
